title: [Mouse Utilities] Add Auto Hide Cursor
summary: The new Auto Hide Cursor utility passes Phase 0 and targeted native, Settings, GPO, and spelling validation. The converged review found idle-detection starvation, incomplete standard-cursor coverage, incorrect GPO version metadata, a WinRT ABI ordering break, and missing UI integration coverage. A current-head request-changes review is drafted.

status.detail: The final fresh Copilot passes produced zero new comments and all Copilot threads are resolved. Targeted builds, 7/7 native tests, and 6/6 Settings tests pass.

review.body_prefix: Thanks for adding Auto Hide Cursor. Before this system-wide cursor replacement feature is ready, please address the idle-timer starvation, cursor coverage, policy metadata, and WinRT ABI concerns below, and add automated Settings integration coverage for the new module.

actions.note: Recheck the upstream head, checks, comments, reviews, and threads; validate the pinned payload; and obtain explicit approval before publishing.

proposed_comments.title: Do not let message traffic starve idle hiding

confidence.rationale: The timer currently runs only after WAIT_TIMEOUT. Continuous queued messages can therefore prevent the independent pointer-idle transition indefinitely; evaluating after every successful wake directly removes that starvation.

proposed_comments.title: Hide every supported standard cursor shape

confidence.rationale: OCR_HELP, OCR_PIN, and OCR_PERSON are standard cursor identifiers on supported Windows versions. Omitting them leaves visible cursor shapes while the utility claims system-wide hiding.

proposed_comments.body:
### Hide every supported standard cursor shape

**Severity:** `medium`

The list omits Help Select, Location Select, and Person Select, so those standard shapes remain visible while the utility is active. Include all supported standard cursor IDs; the descriptive names below also satisfy the repository spelling check.

```suggestion
        inline static constexpr std::array<DWORD, 16> systemCursorIds = {
            32512, // OCR_NORMAL
            32513, // Text select
            32514, // OCR_WAIT
            32515, // OCR_CROSS
            32516, // OCR_UP
            32642, // OCR_SIZENWSE
            32643, // OCR_SIZENESW
            32644, // OCR_SIZEWE
            32645, // OCR_SIZENS
            32646, // OCR_SIZEALL
            32648, // OCR_NO
            32649, // OCR_HAND
            32650, // Working in background
            32651, // OCR_HELP
            32671, // OCR_PIN
            32672, // OCR_PERSON
        };
```

proposed_comments.title: Advertise the correct policy introduction version

confidence.rationale: Auto Hide Cursor is introduced in the 0.101 release train, so the 0.97 reference gives Group Policy administrators incorrect compatibility information.

proposed_comments.body:
### Advertise the correct policy introduction version

**Severity:** `medium`

This policy is new in the current 0.101 release train, but the template advertises it as available since 0.97. Use the current release definition so Group Policy Editor reports accurate compatibility.

```suggestion
      <supportedOn ref="SUPPORTED_POWERTOYS_0_101_0" />
```

proposed_comments.title: Append the new GPO method without shifting WinRT ABI slots

confidence.rationale: Adding a method in the middle of the generated statics interface shifts the vtable position of every subsequent member. Existing additions are appended specifically to preserve binary ordering.

proposed_comments.body:
### Append the new GPO method without shifting WinRT ABI slots

**Severity:** `high`

`GetConfiguredAutoHideCursorEnabledValue` is inserted before existing members in `src/common/GPOWrapper/GPOWrapper.idl`. That shifts the generated WinRT statics-interface slots for `GetConfiguredCursorWrapEnabledValue` and every method after it, which can break mixed-version consumers. Move the new method to the end of the existing method list so all established ABI positions remain unchanged.

proposed_comments.title: Cover the new Settings and worker integration

confidence.rationale: The existing native and serialization tests do not exercise Settings bindings, IPC updates, worker lifecycle, or cursor restoration. Other Mouse Utilities modules have dedicated UI suites for equivalent integration surfaces.

proposed_comments.body:
### Cover the new Settings and worker integration

**Severity:** `medium`

Please add `MouseUtils.UITests.Next` coverage for enabling and disabling Auto Hide Cursor, both trigger toggles and their persisted values, the 1–60 second delay bounds, and worker start/stop/restart behavior. The current unit tests cover state and serialization, but not the Settings bindings, IPC path, or cursor restoration lifecycle introduced by this module.
